newsitem.title: USA: Missouri schools benefit from credit program --S&P.
newsitem.headline: Missouri schools benefit from credit program --S&P.

text.p: Missouri's school credit enhancement program has benefited local districts, which have already issued more in general obligation debt this year than they did in all of 1996, Standard & Poor's reported Monday in its CreditWeek Municipal publication.

In 1996, 69 Missouri school districts used the enhancement program to issue $272.9 million of general obligation bonds and in the first few months of 1997, another 57 districts have sold $299.6 million of GOs under the program, S&P reported.
Missouri's nearly two-year-old program, one of 20 rated by S&P, provides a AA rating for previously unrated or lesser rated issuers giving them pricing advantage and interest rate savings, S&P noted.
The ratings reflect strong statutory and program rules, growing state aid and a requirement that the first dollar of monthly aid go to debt service, S&P said.

"These structural elements translate into a high degree of credit quality," S&P said. "Additional provisions of bankruptcy waiver, investment standards of monies held for debt service, and protection against future claims on state aid by non-program obligations serve to support the AA rating."
